hypothesis: Diffusion Model generates novel samples by reversing noise accumulation, addressing lack of diversity in static generators, to improve generalization across domains
description: The method starts from random noise and iteratively refines it using learned patterns, introducing variation at each step to escape local modes; unlike deterministic generators that produce identical outputs, this stochastic process encourages exploration of underrepresented regions in data space, potentially enhancing robustness and adaptability to new tasks without overfitting to training distributions.

Hypothesis: Diffusion Model generates novel samples by reversing noise accumulation, addressing lack of diversity in static generators, to improve generalization across domains  
Description: The method starts from random noise and iteratively refines it using learned patterns, introducing variation at each step to escape local modes; unlike deterministic generators that produce identical outputs, this stochastic process encourages exploration of underrepresented regions in data space, potentially enhancing robustness and adaptability to new tasks without overfitting to training distributions.

Rules: the hypothesis sentence must have between 20 and 30 words: if the input is short, make it concrete by stating how the method would be applied; if the input is long, condense it to its core idea; begin the hypothesis sentence directly with the method (never with "This study", "This approach", "We", or similar); use plain, neutral language and at most one technical term per noun phrase; do not exaggerate; do not invent results, numbers, datasets, or citations; do not mention how the hypothesis was obtained; output only the two lines.
